name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 6, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:02
p.m., on July 6, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on July 2, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ury

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

City Council Minutes  1  July 6, 2010
 RECESS

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:08 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session item CS1, the City Council
continued their review of the City Manager position. They held discussions with City Manager
Wilberg but there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim July 2010 as Parks and Recreation Month

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Ron Ruef, Chairman of the Community
  Services Commission.

P2.  Presentation by Nadia Babayi of the U.S. Census Bureau recognizing the City of
  Mission Viejo’s efforts in promoting the 2010 Census

  The City Council received the award from Nadia Babayi of the U.S. Census Bureau.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Dan Avery, M.V.: expressed support for the renewal of Waste Management's contract.

Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: discussed Council Member Schlicht's suggestion that the city does not
need the Outlook, Leisure Time, and Annual Report because residents can read them on the web.

Matt Corrigan, M.V.: expressed support for the elimination of lifetime medical benefits for City
Council Members.

Helen Workun, M.V.: shared photographs of No on Measure D signs which were covered in
hand-written obscenities and then thrown into her back yard.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that no one from the city called to tell her that her name appears on the
City Council meeting agenda. She said that she has never sued the city nor is she going to and
she asked the Council Members to stop playing "gotcha" politics.

Stuart Wells, Public Affairs Strategy Manager for San Diego Gas & Electric: introduced himself
as the city's new SDG&E representative and announced that he will be available to answer any
questions on the two agenda items pertaining to SDG&E.

CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Minutes  2  July 6, 2010
 Items 12, 15, 21, and 23 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of June 21, 2010, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register dated June 11, 2010, in the amount of $1,585,051.34

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated June 18, 2010, in the amount of $1,775,572.90

  Ratified the accompanying check register

5.  Microsoft Licensing Renewal Agreement

  Approved issuance of a purchase order to CompuCom for such services for 2010-11 in
  the amount of $66,018.68.

6.  Official Results of the June 8, 2010, Special Municipal Election

  Adopted Resolution 10-35 Reciting the Fact That a Special Municipal Election Was Held
  on June 8, 2010, and Declaring the Results Thereof.

7.  Purchase of Janitorial- Related Paper, Plastic, and Chemical Supplies for City
  Building Facilities
  (1) Awarded primary contract to Clean Source in the amount of $36,875.00; and (2)
  awarded secondary contract to Waxie Sanitary Supply in the amount of $34,711.00.

City Council Minutes  3  July 6, 2010
 8.  Annual Routine Tree Trimming Contract - West Coast Arborists, Inc.

  Approved the Fifth Amendment to the existing contract with West Coast Arborists, Inc.
  to increase the contract in an amount not to exceed $20,000.00 to cover costs associated
  with renovation of Turf Lane Park.

9.  Annual Technical Irrigation Contract

  Approved the Fifth Amendment to the existing contract with A.C. Landscape, Inc. to
  increase the contract in an amount not to exceed $20,000.00 to cover costs associated
  with renovation of Turf Lane Park.

10.  Annual Support for Integrated Library System Software and Hardware for the
  Mission Viejo Library

  Approved Purchase of Annual Support for Integrated Library System Software and
  Hardware for the Mission Viejo Library for FY 2010-11 in the amount of $30,701.40.

11.  Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation, Avery Parkway to Crown Valley
  Parkway (CIP 788)

  (1) Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to PALP, Inc., dba Excel
  Paving Company in the amount of $849,875; and (2) adopted Resolution 10-36
  Amending the Fiscal Year 2010?2011 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement
  Project 788.

13.  Interstate 5 Noise Barrier Scope Summary

  Authorized staff to issue a purchase order to VA Consulting, Inc., in an amount not to
  exceed $137,294 for the subject project.

14.  California Road System Map Updates

  Adopted Resolution 10-37 Approving the Submittal of a Functional Classification
  Change for Local Streets and Roads to the State of California, Department of
  Transportation.

16.  Revised FY 2010-11 Mission Viejo Community Development Agency Budget

  Approved CDA Resolution 2010-04 Adopting a Revised Budget for the Community
  Development Agency (CDA) of the City of Mission Viejo for 2010-11.

17.  Adoption of FY 2010-11 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority

City Council Minutes  4  July 6, 2010
   Adopted CDFA Resolution 2010-03 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo
  Community Development Financing Authority for the 2010-11 Fiscal Year.

18.  Cooperative Agreement No. C-9-0467 Between the Orange County Transportation
  Authority and the City of Mission Viejo for Go Local Bus/Shuttle Service Planning

  Approved Amendment No. 1 to Cooperative Agreement No. C-9-0467 between the
  Orange County Transportation Authority and the City of Mission Viejo for Go Local
  bus/shuttle service planning.

19.  Pavement Management Program: Year 2010 Update

  Received and filed.

20.  Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre - Year 2010 - Phase 1

  (1) Adopted Resolution 10-38 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt
  on Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City
  Council to Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for
  Hearing Protests; (2) instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to
  Destroy Weeds in accordance with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3)
  instructed the City Clerk to set the Public Hearing for August 16, 2010.

22.  Number not used

24.  Personnel Policy Revision - Acting Appointments

  Adopted Resolution No. 10-39 Providing for the Revision of the Personnel Policy on
  Acting Appointments.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

25.  Adoption of the Revised FY 2010-11 City Budget

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 10-40 Adopting a Revised Budget for the City of Mission Viejo for FY
  2010-11 and Appropriating Funds for FY 2010-11; (2) adopt Resolution 10-41,
  Amending the City’s Salary Schedule and Suspending the City’s Current 1%
  Contribution to the 401(a) Defined Contribution Retirement Plan; (3) adopt Resolution
  10-42 Modifying the Employer-Paid Member Contributions to the California Public
  Employees’ Retirement System for City Employees of the Miscellaneous Group; (4)

City Council Minutes  5  July 6, 2010
   adopt Resolution 10-43 Designating a Senior Executive Group and Establishing the
  Employer-Paid Member Contribution to the California Public Employees’ Retirement
  System for Employees of the Senior Executive Group; and (5) adopt Resolution 10-44
  Establishing an Appropriations Limit for FY 2010-11.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

26.  Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program (Fiscal Year 2010-2011
  through Fiscal Year 2016-2017)

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht referred to the last paragraph on page 13 of the staff report,
  where Avery Parkway from I-5 to Marguerite is identified as having the lowest pavement
  condition rating in the city. She asked if staff has any idea when Laguna Niguel will
  move forward with the completion of their project on that street so Mission Viejo can
  complete the resurfacing.

  Consultant Gail Shiomoto-Lohr responded that the City of Laguna Niguel has concluded
  the improvements to Avery under the I-5 bridge. Mission Viejo's Seven-Year CIP
  identifies the Avery improvements as a candidate project for the Fiscal Year 2012-13.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to adopt
  Resolution-45 Adopting a Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program
  Beginning with the 2010?2011 Fiscal Year.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

27.  Integrated Solid Waste Management Services

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Joe Sloan, Sloan Vazquez, discussed contract negotiations and the elements of the
  agreement which have been negotiated with Waste Management.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed opposition to the award of the contract to Waste

City Council Minutes  6  July 6, 2010
   Management. He encouraged senior citizens over the age of 65 to phone Waste
  Management and request the 20% discount allowed by Proposition 218.

  Jason Rush, Ware and Madison Materials: asked the City Council to maintain the current
  contract with Madison Materials for disposal of the city’s construction and demolition
  waste.

  Charissa McAfee, Waste Management: thanked the City Council for the opportunity to
  participate in this process and stated that Waste Management is committed to continuing
  to provide the highest level of service to the residents of Mission Viejo.

  The following presented a written comment in opposition to award of the contract to
  Waste Management: Max and Barbara McDougall.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 10-46 Approving a Franchise Agreement with Waste Management of
  Orange County; and (2) award the franchise agreement for Integrated Solid Waste
  Management Services to U. S. Waste of California, Inc., dba Waste Management of
  Orange County (A10-30) for the period from January 1, 2011, through December 31,
  2018.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

28.  Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  The following expressed opposition to the proposed renovations at the Marguerite Tennis
  Center: Larry Gilbert, M.V.

  Council Member Ury departed at 7:40 p.m. and returned at 7:41 p.m.

  The following expressed support for the proposed renovations at the Marguerite Tennis
  Center: Wil Garcia, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in support of the renovation project: James
  Hruby, M.V. and Kime Goodrum, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in opposition to the renovation project: Max
  and Barbara McDougall, M.V.

City Council Minutes  7  July 6, 2010
   Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1)
  approve the contract bid documents; and (2) authorize staff to advertise for bids for the
  Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

12.  Marguerite Parkway Pavement/Median Rehabilitation, Via Angelina to Trabuco
  Road (CIPs 799, 200 and 206) and La Paz Road Pavement Rehabilitation, Chrisanta
  Drive to Marguerite Parkway (CIP 837)

  Council Member Schlicht asked if American Asphalt can guarantee their work on
  Olympiad before they are paid for this project.

  City Manager Wilberg explained that the problems on Olympiad were related to the
  asphalt material not the contractor’s workmanship.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to award
  the construction contract for the subject project to All American Asphalt, Inc., in the
  amount of $1,383,887, contingent upon the adoption of the revised Fiscal Year 2010-
  2011 Capital Improvement Program Budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

15.  First Amendment to Lease Agreement Between the City and Sprint PCS Assets,
  LLC, in Conjunction with an Existing Wireless Telecommunication Facility on the
  Clock Tower at the YMCA Recreation Center, 27341 Trabuco Circle, in the R
  (Recreation) zone.

  Council Member Schlicht asked about EMF safety levels and asked if anyone is checking
  EMF rating to make sure the towers are within Federal safety guidelines.

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson confirmed that RF study emissions
  are presented along with each application for a new wireless telecommunication facility.

City Council Minutes  8  July 6, 2010
   Council Member Schlicht stated that parents of the children who attend the YMCA
  program should be notified of the wireless communication facility since it is invisible.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  approve and authorize the City Manager to Execute the First Amendment to the Lease
  Amendment.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

21.  Professional Services Agreement for State Legislative Advocacy Services

  Council Member Schlicht noted that this is an agreement for Sacramento lobbyists. She
  was opposed to extending the contract last year and she is still opposed.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness , to
  approve the proposed Professional Services Agreement for State legislative advocacy
  services by Townsend Public Affairs (A10-28) for a total not to exceed amount of
  $60,000 for the period of July 7, 2010, to June 30, 2011.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

23.  City Hall Solar Photo Voltaic Project (CIP 320)

  Council Member Schlicht asked staff if the balance of the grant funds can be used for
  another solar project within the city, for example, at the Murray Center.

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay announced that he will be speaking with
  representatives of the Federal government to see how the city might use the balance of
  the funds.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  award a contract for the subject project to AAA Solar Electric, Inc. in an amount not to
  exceed $584,798.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  9  July 6, 2010
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:15 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:28
p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council Member Ledesma returned to the dais at
8:29 p.m.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

29.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

30.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

31.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San Joaquin
  Hills TCA.

32.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg reminded the City Council that the Lennar/Target land transfer closed
escrow last Friday so the city received its $2 million in park fees.

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley noted that Lennar is moving forward on the residential parcel of that
combined Target/housing property and he takes the investment and development activity as a
good sign for the economy.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

City Council Minutes  10  July 6, 2010
 33.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Ledesma

34.  E-Verify Ordinance Update

  Steve Serra, M.V.: expressed support for the proposed amendments to the ordinance.

  The following presented a written comment in support of the ordinance update: Max and
  Barbara McDougall, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  (1) introduce Ordinance 10-281 Amending and Restating Ordinance No. 07-247, as
  Amended, as Set Forth in Chapter 2.80 of Title 2 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code;
  and (2) direct staff to implement a verification policy with all contractors that are subject
  to the Basic Pilot / E-Verify program.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

35.  Energy and Maintenance Saving Through Additional Light Emitting Diode (LED)
  Usage

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  (1) direct staff to select a test location for installing LED lights on the street lights
  attached to stop lights; and (2) direct staff to estimate cost savings by switching to LED
  lights at all of the intersections with "cobra head" street lights.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

Council Member Ledesma wished his colleagues and residents a good summer.

City Council Minutes  11  July 6, 2010
 Council Member Schlicht

36.  Elimination of Lifetime Healthcare Benefits for the Remaining Eligible Council
  Members

  The following spoke in opposition to Lifetime Medical Benefits for Council Members:
  Larry Gilbert, M.V. and Rhonda Reardon, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in support of the proposal: Max and Barbara
  McDougall, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to lay the item
  on the table.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Ury
  NOES:  Leckness, Ledesma, and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  approve an Amendment to the Council Policies to eliminate current and future council
  members from eligibility in the Mission Viejo Employee Retiree Medical Benefit
  Program.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ury
  ABSENT: None

37.  Marguerite Tennis, Aquatics, and Recreation Center Complex Renovation and
  Expansion Project

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern about parking figures that were listed in the
  Hodge and Associates Mitigated Negative Declaration and asked what recourse the city
  has for accepting a misleading document.

  The following presented a written comment in opposition to the Marguerite Tennis
  Center renovation project: Max and Barbara McDougall, M.V.

Council Member Schlicht announced that she had her traditional root beer float at the Fourth of
July Street Faire; attendance was high and everyone seemed to have a good time. She also
observed the South Orange County Amateur Radio Association Annual Field Day and she

City Council Minutes  12  July 6, 2010
 learned a lot at the event. Council Member Schlicht closed by reading the speech she shared at
the 4th of July Tea Party and she wished everyone a happy summer.

Council Member Ury

38.  Irrevocable Release of the Retiree Medical Benefit

  Council Member Ury asked the City Council to receive and file his Irrevocable Release
  of Retiree Medical Benefits.
39.  Public Release of all Correspondence Between former Council Member Reavis and
  City Staff Regarding her Concerns and Plans for the Lifetime Medical Benefits

  Council Member Ury requested that staff compile emails and correspondence between
  staff and former Council Member Reavis regarding lifetime medical benefits. He noted
  that this is simply a public records request and no action is required on the part of his
  colleagues.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that there is no need to place this on the agenda and it is just a
  waste of staff's time.

40.  Request Former Council Member Reavis to Allow for the Release of all Private
  Communications Between her and City Attorney Curley Regarding Lifetime
  Medical Benefits

  Council Member Ury requested that staff procure communications between former
  Council Member Reavis and the City Attorney and release them publicly. He announced
  that City Attorney Curley has agreed to prepare and execute the release documents at no
  charge to the city.

41.  Direct the City Attorney to Prepare Release Documents for former Council
  Member Reavis to Release the City from Any Further Claim to the Lifetime
  Medical Benefit Both as a Fully Vested Interest and as a Partially Vested One

  Council Member Ury noted that the City Attorney has agreed to ask former Council
  Member Reavis to sign a release of lifetime medical benefits and he looks forward to
  seeing which of these documents are executed.

Council Member Ury expressed disappointment that he was not able to participate in the dunk
tank on the Fourth of July and he wished everyone a very good summer.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness stated that he hopes the lifetime medical benefit discussions are behind
the City Council and he wants the Council to hit the ground running after the summer hiatus. He
would like to see the City Council work on filling the empty big-box stores and he noted that the

City Council Minutes  13  July 6, 2010
 Council Members have to work together and support the city's businesses. Mayor Pro Tem
Leckness stated that these are the things that he was elected to do and he wants to work on
projects that really matter to the city.

Mayor Kelley

42.  Rejection of Retiree Medical Benefits

  Mayor Kelley asked the City Council to receive and file her Irrevocable Release of
  Retiree Medical Benefits.

Mayor Kelley commended the animal shelter staff and the Dedicated Animal Welfare Group
volunteers who put together a very successful DAWG Walk and Pet Faire. It was a wonderful,
positive event and it raised money to help DAWG continue providing medical services to the
animals in our city. She stated that the Mission Viejo Activities Committee outdid themselves
with this year’s Fourth of July Street Faire. She believes it was the largest crowd the city has
ever seen and it is put on by a very small group of volunteers who give their time and talents for
the benefit of our residents. Mayor Kelley discussed her role administering the dunk tank and she
commended Mayor Pro Tem Leckness for serving three half-hour shifts inside the dunk tank.
She also thanked Castille Elementary School Principal Laura Lyon for participating in the dunk
tank. She noted that the booth raised $664 for the Relay for Life and she thanked the Mission
Viejo Activities Committee and all the volunteers who make this wonderful event possible.
Mayor Kelley announced the upcoming Support our Troops Car Wash on Saturday, July 17,
2010, from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. in the civic center parking lot. The suggested donation is $20
and most of the money helps to send our adopted Marines to the Marine Corps ball. Donations
also help those in need and to highlight that, Mayor Kelley read a letter from Corporal Bravo
who thanked the city for facilitating a trip home when his father was very ill. She noted that the
City’s participation in these events is meaningful and makes a difference in many lives. Mayor
Kelley announced that the city received complaints about the Tea Party gathering on the Fourth
of July due to the use of amplifiers. She noted that the city did not issue permits for
amplification so this was a violation and the city is sorry for the disturbance. Mayor Kelley
announced that the Community of Character word for the month of July is fairness.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:10 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Les Cromwell and Debbie Allison,
to Monday, August 16, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of August 16, 2010

City Council Minutes  14  July 6, 2010
